Credit-bearing

Courses or programs that award academic credit that can count toward a university degree or certificate.

Course certificate

A digital certificate you receive after finishing the course requirements. It records course completion but is not the same as university academic credit unless explicitly stated.

Will I get a course certificate after completing a course?

Yes, you will receive a course certificate after completing all the items in the course. There are select courses that do not offer a certificate. It is generally indicated on the course description page where you enroll.

How many courses should I take per term?

Most students take 1–2 courses per 8-week term depending on their schedule. 2 courses per term are required to be considered “full-time” enrolled.

Free, Career-Focused Microcredential Courses

Ease into your academic journey with free 4-week courses in Organizational Leadership, led by expert Texas Tech faculty. Featuring career-enhancing themes such as team leadership and career development, these bite-size courses allow you to kickstart your educational and career goals. Upon completion, earn a digital badge for each course, demonstrating your achievements and providing credit conversion options for your future degree completion.

Coming Soon

We are currently piloting and developing additional opportunities for learners to earn microcredentials developed by Texas Tech faculty. Courses cover a range of topics spanning communication, business, technology, leadership, finance, and human resources. With a commitment to offering diverse and impactful learning experiences, we are confident that you will find a microcredential program that precisely meets your needs.

Stay tuned for the full list of microcredentials, launching soon!

Curriculum

The curriculum for the Master of Engineering program consists of 30 semester credit hours of coordinated graduate level course work. No more than 12 credit hours (4 courses) can be taken in any single engineering discipline, e.g., Industrial Engineering or Mechanical Engineering.

The program allows up to six hours of course work to be taken outside of engineering, upon the approval of the graduate advisor.

Every candidate for a master's degree is required to pass a final comprehensive examination.In the final semester, students must take the Master’s report course (ENGR6330) which serves as their comprehensive exam requirement for graduation.

Transfer of Courses

Students may be permitted to transfer up to six credit hours of relevant engineering coursework from another university graduate program upon approval of the Graduate School. All transfer courses are subject to the same time limitations as courses taken in the program (a maximum of six years from the first course in the plan of study until graduation).

I enrolled in a course that my advisor later told me that I am no longer required to take, can I withdraw and enroll in another course?

Yes, you may withdraw from the course you are no longer required to take and enroll in another course during specific parts of the term. However, it is essential to understand the financial and academic impacts of dropping the course. Here are the steps to withdraw:

Step 1: Make sure to discuss the situation with your Online Student Advocate.

Step 2: Login to Raiderlink.

Step 3: Click on "My Student Dashboard".

Step 4: Click on "Registrar Forms".

Step 5: Click on "New Registrar Request".

Step 6: Click on "Student Withdraw".

If a student plans to remain enrolled in at least one other course for the term, they would follow the process for dropping a course. withdrawal is for situations where the student is dropping all courses and will have zero hours for the term.

Remember to withdraw only from the specific term you wish to drop to zero hours. Before making any changes, it's advisable to check the financial consequences with your financial aid advisor. If you need further assistance, don't hesitate to reach out to your Online Student Advocate.

Software Engineering Specialization (The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology) - course 1

Step 1: Software Engineering: Modeling Software Systems using UML – course 1 – 28 hours

Step 2: Software Engineering: Implementation and Testing – course 2 – 19 hours

Step 3: Software Engineering: Software Design and Project Management – course 3 – 19 hours

Step 4: Other equivalent online certification (e.g., Cisco certification) with prior approval of graduate advisor

Transfer Coursework

Transfer credit may be accepted from another university as long as the following conditions are met:

Step 1: A final grade of 'B' or higher was earned in the course. Students are required to submit an official transcript submitted to the Graduate School.

Step 2: The course was not taken by correspondence.

Step 3: The inclusion of the course satisfies degree plan requirements.

Step 4: The course is approved by the Graduate Advisor, Graduate Coordinator, and (if applicable) the student's thesis advisor.

Step 5: A Texas Tech University course corresponds to the transferred course.

Step 6: The course is from a computer science or similar program.

A MS student may only transfer up to 6 hours (two classes).

Texas Tech University has designed this curriculum to provide graduates with the advanced knowledge and skills needed to succeed in this demanding field. This degree builds on foundational knowledge gained in associate programs, combined with professional experience, to deliver a strong upper-level core based on all-hazards principles.

Students study hazard identification and risk assessment, emergency planning and preparedness, incident command, disaster recovery, continuity planning, mitigation strategies, resilience building, leadership, crisis communication, and policy, legal and ethical issues. Courses are delivered entirely online in an asynchronous 8-week format.

The program emphasizes real-world application through case studies, simulations, peer discussions and a capstone project.
